rejected_videos.reason: No clean standalone, prerequisite-safe segment was found. The redirect implementation at 283–431 depends on routing code and a Riverpod-based project introduced earlier; Riverpod is not in this path's allowed knowledge. The listener explanation at 431–643 relies on a previous video's custom service/controller architecture and introduces Firestore service updates at 530–535, a blocked topic. The brief redirect recap at 779–798 supports session-dependent destination selection, but refers to existing code without supplying its setup or completing a standalone example. The transcript does not establish returning null or the original path for permitted navigation (f2), keeping sign-in allowed without a self-redirect loop (f3), or retaining backend authorization as the security boundary (f4). These are coverage gaps, not confirmed factual contradictions.

No clean standalone segment serves this concept. At 358–382, the explanation incorrectly attributes document creation to obtaining a document reference: calling doc/document only obtains a reference; the subsequent write creates the document. This is a factual error, not merely missing coverage. The demo also uses legacy document()/setData() APIs, never demonstrates get() with absent-document/data checks (f2), and never explains ordinary-set overwrite semantics or merge preservation (f3–f4). Its write implementation depends on a collection reference and project setup introduced previously. The final console demonstration confirms registration-created fields, but does not demonstrate the required document-backed read/edit/write workflow.

No standalone segment covers the required document read/write facts f1–f5. The video explains collections and document fields and demonstrates only a collection reference; it never addresses a document by ID, reads a DocumentSnapshot, checks absent data, writes a payload, demonstrates merge preservation, or awaits write completion. It defers document operations to the next lesson at 370 seconds. It also makes a technically incorrect claim at 326–348 seconds that obtaining a collection reference creates a nonexistent collection; a reference alone does not create stored data. The opening setup additionally instructs enabling unrestricted test-mode access rather than working under supplied security rules.

No verifiable standalone segment covers the target using the supplied messaging setup. The explanation at 287–306 supports foreground notifications not appearing by default (f3), but does not teach the onMessage subscription, payload and metadata access, or subscription cancellation (f1, f2, f4). The messaging-service chapter at 563–792 is largely music-only captions; its code and prerequisite safety cannot be established from the supplied evidence. The foreground test at 875–918 depends on a token and custom services established earlier, so it is not standalone. It demonstrates a local notification rather than establishing the specified in-app response.

No clean standalone range adequately teaches the required foreground-message handling. The explanation beginning at 472 demonstrates onMessage and reads notification title/body, but never teaches RemoteMessage.data (f2), the Android/iOS default of no visible foreground notification (f3), or cancellation of the owned subscription on disposal (f4). At 558 the explanation moves into notification-detail navigation, making the completed example dependent on an excluded responsibility. The runtime demonstration also interleaves receipt with navigation. There are explicit technical inaccuracies elsewhere in the video: at 1109–1112 it claims the device's messaging token is always the same, although FCM tokens can rotate; at 978–995 it incorrectly presents enabling notification-display permission as necessary for receiving messages, conflating display authorization with foreground message delivery. These are source-quality problems, not merely missing coverage.

The relevant chapter (68–259s) misleadingly attributes avoided recreation and rebuilds to extracting a widget-returning method into a widget class alone. The reported reduction from approximately 300 to 57 builds does not establish re-recording the same interaction with unchanged visible behavior. The transcript also does not teach localizing setState, const configurations, provider select, or Consumer's child argument. Later chapters address other performance concerns rather than the required rebuild-scope fix.

Reject for technical accuracy and current-workflow mismatch. At 1231–1240, the video says review 'can take up to 48 hours' and that approval results in Play Store listing. The demonstrated rollout workflow does not explain Changes not yet sent for review or sending changes through Publishing overview (f2). It also omits rejection recovery (f4), managed publishing and verification of published availability (f5), and iOS build processing (f6). Although 1242–1251 correctly distinguishes an app still in review from a published app (f3), this brief status observation is the conclusion of an existing-release walkthrough, not a sufficient standalone submission mini-lesson.
